Girls (TV series) :: Topics explored :: chunk_0002
*Girls* explores several topics across its six seasons. Dunham explains *Girls* never started with an "overt, political, or even [exact] artistic mission statement."[[14]](#cite_note-CL-14) While the primary themes in the television show explore interpersonal relationships—particularly female friendship and romantic affairs—New York City culture, coming-of-age struggle, career, mental health, artistic boundaries and self-reflection, Dunham states the show was never "stuck in any specific formula."[[14]](#cite_note-CL-14) She also noted "the series reflects a part of the population that hasn’t previously been seen on either film or television and fills the gap between the characters on *[Sex and the City](/wiki/Sex_and_the_City "Sex and the City")* and the [CW](/wiki/The_CW "The CW")’s *[Gossip Girl](/wiki/Gossip_Girl "Gossip Girl")*."[[15]](#cite_note-15) The series ultimately explores how significantly flawed, unlikable, morally ambiguous characters in their twenties navigate the challenges of adulthood and learn to embrace their imperfections.[[16]](#cite_note-16)[[17]](#cite_note-17)[[18]](#cite_note-18)

fanoutqa_027147.x:
Human papillomavirus infection :: Conditions and diseases :: Cancer :: Cervical cancer :: chunk_0006
Nearly all cases of [cervical cancer](/wiki/Cervical_cancer "Cervical cancer") are associated with HPV infection, with two types, HPV16 and HPV18, present in 70% of cases.[[1]](#cite_note-who-cervicalc2-1)[[9]](#cite_note-CDC2015Can-9)[[23]](#cite_note-Baseman-23)[[58]](#cite_note-58)[[59]](#cite_note-Ault_2006-59)[[60]](#cite_note-60) In 2012, twelve HPV types were considered carcinogenic for cervical cancer by the [International Agency for Research on Cancer](/wiki/International_Agency_for_Research_on_Cancer "International Agency for Research on Cancer"): 16, 18, 31, 33, 35, 39, 45, 51, 52, 56, 58, and 59.[[61]](#cite_note-:51-61) One study found that 74% of squamous cell carcinomas and 78% of adenocarcinomas tested positive for HPV types 16 or 18.[[62]](#cite_note-pmid17131323-62) Persistent HPV infection increases the risk for developing cervical carcinoma. Individuals who have an increased incidence of these types of infection are women with HIV/AIDS, who are at a 22-fold increased risk of cervical cancer.[[63]](#cite_note-pmid23199960-63)[[64]](#cite_note-pmid23259425-64)

The carcinogenic HPV types in cervical cancer belong to the [alphapapillomavirus](/wiki/Alphapapillomavirus "Alphapapillomavirus") genus. They can be grouped further into HPV [clades](/wiki/Clade "Clade").[[65]](#cite_note-65) The two major carcinogenic HPV clades, alphapapillomavirus-9 (A9) and alphapapillomavirus-7 (A7), contain [HPV16](/wiki/Papillomaviridae "Papillomaviridae") and [HPV18](/wiki/Papillomaviridae "Papillomaviridae"), respectively.[[66]](#cite_note-66) These two HPV clades were shown to have different effects on tumour molecular characteristics and patient prognosis, with clade A7 being associated with more aggressive pathways and an inferior prognosis.[[67]](#cite_note-67)

fanoutqa_013579.x:
The Little Prince :: Background :: Reception :: chunk_0015
Many of the book's initial reviewers were flummoxed by the fable's multi-layered story line and its morals,[[8]](#cite_note-New_Yorker-2014.04.29-9) perhaps expecting a significantly more conventional story from one of France's leading writers. Its publisher had anticipated such reactions to a work that fell neither exclusively into a children's nor adults' literature classification. *[The New York Times](/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")* reviewer wrote shortly before its publication "What makes a good children's book? ... *The Little Prince*, which is a fascinating fable for grown-ups [is] of conjectural value for boys and girls of 6, 8 and 10. [It] may very well be a book on the order of *[Gulliver's Travels](/wiki/Gulliver%27s_Travels "Gulliver's Travels")*, something that exists on two levels"; "Can you clutter up a narrative with paradox and irony and still hold the interest of 8 and 10-year olds?" Notwithstanding the story's duality, the review added that major portions of the story would probably still "capture the imagination of any child."[[77]](#cite_note-NYTimes-1943.04.06-86) Addressing whether it was written for children or adults, [Reynal & Hitchcock](/wiki/Reynal_%26_Hitchcock "Reynal & Hitchcock") promoted it ambiguously, saying that as far as they were concerned "it's the new book by Saint-Exupéry", adding to its dustcover "There are few stories which in some way, in some degree, change the world forever for their readers. This is one."[[58]](#cite_note-ThreeTomatoes-64)

Others were not shy in offering their praise. Austin Stevens, also of *The New York Times*, stated that the story possessed "...large portions of the Saint-Exupéry philosophy and poetic spirit. In a way it's a sort of [credo](/wiki/Credo "Credo")."[[55]](#cite_note-NYTimes-1942.12.06-59) P. L. He finished the game with 28 points.[[190]](#cite_note-190) On November 26, 2017, Anthony passed [Ray Allen](/wiki/Ray_Allen "Ray Allen") on the NBA all-time scoring list and moved to 23rd place.[[191]](#cite_note-191) On December 11, 2017, Anthony passed [Vince Carter](/wiki/Vince_Carter "Vince Carter") for 22nd on the NBA all-time scoring list.[[192]](#cite_note-192)

On January 27, 2018, Anthony became the 21st NBA player to score 25,000 career points.[[193]](#cite_note-193) In addition, he has 1,693 playoff points.[[194]](#cite_note-194)
On March 19, 2018, in a 132–125 victory over the [Toronto Raptors](/wiki/Toronto_Raptors "Toronto Raptors"), Anthony scored 15 points to up his career total to 25,289, thereby moving past [Reggie Miller](/wiki/Reggie_Miller "Reggie Miller") into 19th place in the NBA career scoring ladder.[[195]](#cite_note-195)

Main article: [Congress of State](/wiki/Congress_of_State "Congress of State")

The Congress of State is the government of the country and wields the executive power. It is composed by a variable number of Secretaries of State, which by law cannot exceed the number of 10, that are appointed by the Grand and General Council at the beginning of the legislature. Because of this fact, also the areas of competence of the various Secretaries are not fixed, as some could be merged depending on the number of Secretaries. The law identifies 10 sectors of the public administration for which the secretaries are politically responsible:

Aegean cat

The Aegean is a cat of [Greek](/wiki/Greece "Greece") origin that has been developed since the 1990s by the Feline Federation of Greece, using cats from the [Cyclades](/wiki/Cyclades "Cyclades"). The name comes from the fact that the cats were originally found around the [Aegean Sea](/wiki/Aegean_Sea "Aegean Sea").[[2]](#cite_note-cats101-aegean-2) They are considered a national treasure of Greece.[[2]](#cite_note-cats101-aegean-2) Aegean cats are a [landrace](/wiki/Landrace "Landrace"), and are one of the oldest distinct populations of the domestic cat.[[2]](#cite_note-cats101-aegean-2) They have an affinity for fishing and water, and are numerous in Greek fishing ports.[[2]](#cite_note-cats101-aegean-2) It is a medium-sized, muscular cat[[2]](#cite_note-cats101-aegean-2) with a lighter European or Continental type body, medium-sized round paws, and green almond-shaped eyes.[[2]](#cite_note-cats101-aegean-2) The coat is always two or three colors, one of which is always white.[[2]](#cite_note-cats101-aegean-2) The breed is mostly free from common feline diseases.[[2]](#cite_note-cats101-aegean-2)
